(“Amentum” or the “Company”) (NYSE: AMTM), a leading advanced engineering and technology company, today announced results for the year ended October 2, 2026 and issued guidance for fiscal year 2027. “Amentum closed fiscal year 2026 with strong execution, delivering 50 basis points of margin expansion, increasing earnings per share and free cash flow by 13%, securing $17 billion in contract awards, and completing all major integration milestones,” said Amentum Chief Executive Officer John Heller. “As we enter fiscal year 2027, we remain focused on accelerating organic growth, driving operational excellence across the enterprise, and aligning the business with long-term demand trends. Combined with a disciplined capital allocation strategy, including our newly authorized $500 million share repurchase program, these priorities support our continued focus on creating long-term shareholder value.” Summary Operating Results Three Months Ended Year Ended (in millions, except per share data) October 2, 2026 October 3, 2025 % Change October 2, 2026 October 3, 2025 % Change GAAP Measures: Revenues $3,620 $3,925 (8%) $13,825 $14,393 (4%) Operating income $187 $135 39% $648 $480 35% Net income $174 $40 335% $338 $66 412% Diluted earnings per share $0.71 $0.16 344% $1.38 $0.27 411% Non-GAAP Measures 1 : Adjusted EBITDA 1 $304 $300 1% $1,132 $1,104 3% Adjusted EBITDA Margin 1 8.4% 7.7% +70 bps 8.2% 7.7% +50 bps Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) 1 $0.71 $0.63 13% $2.51 $2.22 13% Free Cash Flow 1 $370 $261 42% $583 $516 13% 1 – Non-GAAP financial measures should be considered in addition to, but not as a substitute for, the information provided in accordance with GAAP. GAAP Results Fourth quarter revenues decreased 8% year-over-year driven by a 9% impact from an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, partially offset by the ramp-up of new contract awards. For the year, revenues decreased by 4% driven by a 5% impact that includes an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, the transition of certain contracts from consolidated to unconsolidated joint ventures, and fiscal year 2025 divestitures as well as impacts from the government shutdown; partially offset by the ramp-up of new contract awards and growth on existing programs. Fourth quarter and full year operating income increased as a result of strong 1 operational performance and decreased intangible amortization expense. Net income and diluted earnings per share improved year-over-year, supported by higher operating income and lower interest expense. Non-GAAP Results Adjusted EBITDA increased 1% for the fourth quarter and 3% for the full year driven by continued progress on our margin expansion initiatives including a favorable mix shift and strong operational performance. Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share increased primarily as a result of the strong operational performance and lower interest expense. Digital Solutions revenues decreased 2% in the fourth quarter driven by a 10% impact from an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, partially offset by the ramp-up of new contract awards in critical digital infrastructure and space systems and technologies. For the year, revenues increased 3% driven by the ramp-up of new contract awards and growth on existing programs; partially offset by a 4% impact that includes an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 and the fiscal year 2025 divestiture of Rapid Solutions. Adjusted EBITDA increased 1% for the fourth quarter and full year as a result of strong program performance and the increased revenue volume, respectively. Global Engineering Solutions revenues decreased 12% in the fourth quarter driven by a 8% impact from an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 as well as the expected ramp-down of historical programs. For the year, revenues decreased by 9% driven by a 5% impact that includes an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, the transition of certain contracts from consolidated to unconsolidated joint ventures, and a fiscal year 2025 divestiture as well as the expected ramp-down of other historical programs. Adjusted EBITDA increased 2% in the fourth quarter and 4% in the full year as a result of continued progress on our margin expansion initiatives, favorable contract mix, and strong program performance. Cash Flow Summary In the fourth quarter, Amentum generated $392 million of net cash from operating activities and used $24 million and $303 million in investing and financing activities, respectively. Net cash provided by operating activities was driven by strong cash earnings, disciplined working capital management, and reflects one less pay cycle compared to the prior year quarter. Net cash used in investing activities included $22 million in capital expenditures. Net cash used in financing activities consisted primarily of $287 million in voluntary principal payment on the Term Loan B. As of October 2, 2026, Amentum had $521 million in cash and cash equivalents and $3,574 million of gross debt. With net leverage reduced to 2.7x, Amentum has strengthened its financial position, providing greater flexibility for disciplined and opportunistic deployment. Share Repurchase Authorization Subsequent to quarter end, the Company’s Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to $500 million of the Company’s common stock. The share repurchase program provides additional flexibility to deploy capital as part of the Company’s disciplined capital allocation strategy. 2 Backlog and Contract Awards As of October 2, 2026, the Company had total backlog of $48.3 billion, which includes an approximately $1.5 billion de-booking related to contract changes at NASA, compared with $47.1 billion as of October 3, 2025, an increase of 2.4% driven by $15.0 billion in net bookings and 1.1x book-to-bill. Funded backlog as of October 2, 2026 was $6.0 billion, compared with $5.6 billion as of October 3, 2025, an increase of 8.0%. Notable Highlights • NGA Integrated Campus Support (NICS) – The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) awarded Amentum an $800 million ten-year contract to deliver technology-enabled solutions that maximize the performance of critical facilities and systems at NGA Washington. The award builds on Amentum’s successful track record of supporting critical infrastructure for national security missions at NGA and across the U.S. government and its allies across the globe. • Navy Integrated Training Environment (NITE) 2 – The U.S. Navy awarded Amentum a new $700 million five-year contract to provide comprehensive operations and engineering solutions for the Navy’s live, virtual, and constructive integrated environment. Under this contract, Amentum will use secure AI and data analytics to enhance maintenance and operations, improve system readiness, and modernize systems for complex training scenarios. • Australia Nuclear Submarine Shipyard Program – The Australian Naval Infrastructure (ANI) selected an Amentum-led joint venture as its Capability Partner to support the delivery of a nuclear-powered submarine construction yard in South Australia, providing program and construction management. This ten-year program reinforces Amentum’s position as a trusted industry partner, leveraging its extensive global nuclear experience in waterfront infrastructure, waste management, and regulatory in support of supporting global nuclear capabilities. • U.S. Army Germany Site Operations – The U.S. Army awarded Amentum a new $375 million single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract with a six-year ordering period to strengthen U.S. Army mission readiness across 21 installations in Germany. Through this award, Amentum will leverage its global expertise and advanced digital solutions to enhance operational efficiency, modernize installation support, and enable mission-critical operations. • U.K. Nuclear Infrastructure & Remediation Solutions – The United Kingdom nuclear site operator Sellafield Ltd selected an Amentum-led joint venture as a preferred supplier for the nuclear Projects and Asset Care Execution (PACE) program valued up to $2.8 billion over an initial duration of nine years and an optional six-year extension. Amentum will support spent fuel management and retrievals mission through its full lifecycle capabilities, including engineering and design, installation, plant modification, project management and ongoing asset care. Formal award of the framework agreement will follow when final contractual arrangements are concluded. • Navy Counter-Unmanned Systems (C-UxS) – The U.S. Navy awarded Amentum a $145 million single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract with a five-year ordering period to support the U.S. Navy’s modernization of advanced counter-unmanned systems through research, development, testing, and integration of next-generation technologies to enhance operational capabilities. • Classified Intelligence Awards – Amentum was awarded over $350 million in intelligence contracts, including an award supporting enterprise IT and operational objectives to deliver systems engineering, network and infrastructure support, cybersecurity, and platform integration. About Amentum Amentum is a global leader in advanced engineering and technology solutions, trusted by the United States and its allies to address the most complex challenges in science, security and sustainability. Our people apply boundless imagination to challenge convention. Safety, collaboration and well-being are integral to our success. Headquartered in Chantilly, Virginia, we have over 45,000 employees in more than 70 countries across all 7 continents. Visit us at amentum.com to learn how we advance the future together. In addition to the above non-GAAP financial measures, the Company has included backlog, net bookings, and book-to-bill in this release. Backlog is an operational measure representing the estimated amount of future revenues to be recognized under negotiated contracts, and net bookings represent the change in backlog between reporting periods plus reported revenues for the period. Book-to-bill represents net bookings divided by reported revenues for the same period. We believe these metrics are useful for investors because they are an important measure of business development performance and are used by management to conduct and evaluate its business during its regular review of operating results. UNAUDITED NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES The presentation and discussion of Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Diluted EPS, Free Cash Flow, and Net Leverage are not measures of financial performance under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles in the United States (“GAAP”). These non-GAAP measures should be considered only as supplements to, and should not be considered in isolation or used as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. Management believes these non-GAAP measures, when read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP and the reconciliations herein to the most directly comparable GAAP measures, provide useful information in assessing trends in our ongoing operating performance and may provide greater visibility in understanding the long-term financial performance of the Company. The computation of non-GAAP measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies, thus limiting their use for comparability. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders adjusted for interest expense and other, net, provision for income taxes, depreciation and amortization, and excludes the following discrete items: • Acquisition, transaction, and integration costs – Represents acquisition, transaction and integration costs, including severance, retention, and other adjustments related to acquisition and integration activities. • Amortization of intangibles – Represents the amortization of intangible assets. • Divestitures – Represents divestiture gains and losses. • Loss on extinguishment of debt – Represents the write-off of debt discount and debt issuance costs as a result of debt modifications. • Utilization of certain fair market value adjustments assigned in purchase accounting – Represents the periodic utilization of the fair market value adjustments assigned to certain equity method investments and non-controlling interests based on the remaining period of performance for the related contract. • Stock-based compensation – Represents non-cash compensation expenses recognized for stock-based arrangements. Adjusted EBITDA Margin is defined as Adjusted EBITDA divided by revenues. Adjusted Net Income is defined as GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders excluding the discrete items listed under Adjusted EBITDA and the related tax impacts. Adjusted Diluted EPS is defined as Adjusted Net Income divided by diluted weighted average number of common shares outstanding. Free Cash Flow is defined as GAAP cash flow provided by operating activities less purchases of property and equipment. For fiscal year 2026, Free Cash Flow was $583 million, consisting of $627 million of GAAP cash flow provided by operating activities less $44 million of purchases of property and equipment. Net Leverage is defined as GAAP total debt (excluding unamortized original issue discount and deferred financing costs) less cash and cash equivalents, divided by last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA, which is a non-GAAP measure. For fiscal year 2026, Net Leverage was 2.7x, consisting of $3,574 million of total debt less $521 million of cash and cash equivalents, divided by the last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA of $1,132 million. 9 AMENTUM HOLDINGS, INC.
